title: The tie set count for mixed prime parking functions and its dependence on the two parameters
author: Pamela E. Harris, Selvi Kara, Erin McNicholas, Kathryn Nyman and Mei Yin
work: On statistics of prime parking functions, Lukasiewicz paths, and quasisymmetric functions
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 6.4 of the article (source label thm:Tie_Set_count_mixed, source0.tex lines 1276--1279), the mixed-parameter tie set count for prime parking functions: for $m\neq\ell$ and prescribed sets $S\subseteq[n-1]$ of tie positions split between the two kinds of steps, the number of prime parking functions with that tie set is given by the stated closed formula. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 29-line proof at source0.tex lines 1287--1315. H2: the proof is a genuine bijective enumeration with two interacting parameters rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must set up the correspondence between the tie set of a prime parking function and the positions of the horizontal and vertical steps of the associated Lukasiewicz path, count the words with the prescribed multiset of steps by a multinomial argument, and then impose the two parameter-dependent constraints that single out the prime parking functions, which is what produces the closed formula. Reproducing that mixed two-parameter enumeration is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
